blocks.text: Several kinds of formula are used to represent organic compounds.

items: Molecular formula: the actual number of atoms of each element in one molecule, e.g. butane C4H10, ethanoic (acetic) acid C2H4O2, ethanol C2H6O. It does not show how the atoms are joined, so different compounds can share one: ethanol and methoxymethane are both C2H6O.
Empirical formula: the smallest whole-number ratio of the atoms of each element, e.g. butane (C4H10) is C2H5 and ethanoic acid (C2H4O2) is CH2O.
Structural formula: shows the sequence in which the atoms are joined as well as their numbers.
Displayed (graphical) formula: shows every bond between the atoms, including the type of bond and the position of the functional groups.

Condensed (linear) formula: the displayed formula written on one line; single bonds are left out, while branches, functional groups, multiple bonds and repeated CH2 groups are shown, e.g. CH3(CH2)2CH3 (butane), CH3CH2OH (ethanol), CH3COOH (ethanoic acid).

Skeletal (bond-line) formula: the symbols of carbon and hydrogen and the C-H bonds are removed. Carbon-carbon bonds are lines meeting at angles; each corner or line end is a carbon with enough H atoms to make four bonds. Double and triple bonds and functional groups are shown, e.g. ethanol is a short line with OH at one end.

blocks.alt: A table with rows for butane and ethanoic acid and columns for the molecular formula (C4H10; C2H4O2), empirical formula (C2H5; CH2O), displayed formula (every C-H, C-C, C=O, C-O and O-H bond drawn), condensed formula (CH3(CH2)2CH3; CH3COOH) and skeletal formula (a zigzag of three lines; a line to a carbon with C=O and OH).
blocks.caption: Five ways of writing the formulae of butane and ethanoic acid (original table for this topic).
blocks.long_description: The same compound can be written in several ways. The molecular formula counts the atoms, the empirical formula gives their simplest ratio, the displayed formula shows every bond, the condensed formula fits on one line, and the skeletal formula shows only the carbon framework and functional groups.

items: Write condensed formulae for ethanol and methoxymethane. Are they isomers?
